clinician.trajectory_summary: A 19-year-old Nigerian female presented with a 2-month history of recurrent headache, fever, easy fatiguability, and breathlessness. She had been previously treated at a private hospital for presumed typhoid fever and malaria with intravenous medications and received 3 units of blood transfusion for symptomatic anaemia. Symptoms recurred 3 days prior to presentation at Olabisi Onabanjo University Teaching Hospital. On examination, she was severely pale with slight jaundice, but had no lymphadenopathy, no bleeding manifestations, no hepatosplenomegaly, and a clinically clear chest. Complete blood count on admission revealed severe anaemia (PCV 10.8%), normal WBC count (4.1 × 10⁹/L) with lymphocytosis (78%), and thrombocytopenia (50 × 10⁹/L). Peripheral blood smear showed normocytic normochromic red blood cells with nucleated RBCs, immature mononuclear cells with cytoplasmic blebs, and giant platelets. Bone marrow aspiration yielded a dry tap, necessitating bone marrow biopsy. Bone marrow imprint demonstrated increased immature mononuclear cells (>90% of nucleated cells) with abundant basophilic cytoplasm containing vacuoles, hyperchromatic and pleomorphic nuclei, and cytoplasmic blebs. Immunophenotyping of peripheral blood performed by Safety Molecular Pathology Laboratory, Enugu, showed positivity for CD33, CD41, and CD61, confirming the diagnosis of Acute Megakaryoblastic Leukaemia (AML-M7). Induction chemotherapy with cytarabine and daunorubicin (7+3) regimen was initiated. Repeat bone marrow aspiration on day 7 of induction therapy showed blasts <5%, indicating a good response to treatment.

Complete blood count on admission: PCV 10.8%, WBC 4.1 × 10⁹/L (Neutrophil 18.3%, Lymphocyte 78%, Mid 3.4%), Platelets 50 × 10⁹/L
Peripheral blood smear: normocytic normochromic RBCs with nucleated RBCs, immature mononuclear cells with cytoplasmic blebs, and giant platelets

Bone marrow imprint: increased immature mononuclear cells (>90% of nucleated cells) with abundant basophilic cytoplasm containing vacuoles, hyperchromatic and pleomorphic nuclei, and cytoplasmic blebs
Immunophenotyping of peripheral blood shows positivity for CD33, CD41, and CD61, confirming AML-M7
Induction chemotherapy initiated with cytarabine and daunorubicin (7+3) regimen
Repeat bone marrow aspiration on day 7 of induction showed blasts <5%, indicating good response to treatment
